articles.title: Carney Rallies Remain Vote in Alberta
articles.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney urged voters in Alberta to reject separatism in a referendum next week.

articles.title: IEA Agrees to Release of Outstanding 100MM Oil Barrels
articles.description: The International Energy Agency said that member countries agreed to complete the release of 100 million barrels of oil that are still outstanding from an intervention in March.

articles.title: When Will Global Gas Demand Peak?
articles.description: GlobalData offered its view in a statement sent to Rigzone this week.

articles.title: US FERC proposes blanket permit programme for LNG facilities
articles.description: The US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) has put forward the first blanket authorisation programme for liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities through a unanimously backed Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NOPR).

articles.title: OPEC+ Meets on Sidelines of Saudi Conference
articles.description: 'The Ministers reviewed market conditions', a statement posted on OPEC's website said.

articles.title: BW Energy reports 8–9mbbl find in Dussafu appraisal wells in Gabon
articles.description: BW Energy has announced that recent appraisal drilling on the Dussafu field offshore Gabon has identified commercial oil volumes, with an estimated combined gross recovery of approximately 8-9 million barrels (mbbl).

articles.title: Currie Calls Brent 'Vibe Contract' Out of Step with Energy
articles.description: The world's most important oil benchmark has become little more than a 'vibe contract', according to Wall Street veteran Jeff Currie.

articles.title: China Builds Gas Buffer for Winter
articles.description: China has stockpiled enough natural gas to meet winter demand, according to analysts.

articles.title: Essar Oil & Gas wins five new CBM blocks across three Indian states
articles.description: Indian coal bed methane (CBM) operator Essar Oil & Gas has been awarded five exploration blocks covering approximately 1,281km2 across West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana in India.

articles.title: Deadly Airstrikes Expose Growing Battle Over Sudan’s Gold
articles.description: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict Air strikes on October 10 killed at least 72 artisanal gold miners at Shamal al-Wadi, in the far north of Sudan's Red Sea state, along a border Egypt is policing to control a gold trade it now dominates. Survivors put the toll above 200. Miners and Sudanese rights groups blame Egyptian aircraft, and no government has claimed the strikes. Egypt treats the disputed area as its own territory and says its operations against illegal prospecting stayed inside its borders. It is the second deadly raid on the same area…

articles.title: Trump's Oil Price Strategy Faces Two Major Tests This Weekend
articles.description: Two Trump decisions will set this weekend's energy risk, and in both he is giving up leverage to chase lower pump prices before November 3. The first is to keep U.S. firepower out of Saudi Arabia's war with the Houthis. The Houthis hit Aramco's Dhahran headquarters on Tuesday night and have kept Riyadh's main airport shut until Saturday, and Washington's rule since September is that it stays out as long as the Houthis hit only Saudi targets. The second is the license for Russian diesel. It faces its first test on October 18, the deadline in the…

articles.title: Data Centers Drive Surge in India’s Renewable Power Demand
articles.description: Plans for huge data center buildouts in India are set to hike clean energy demand in the country, and local renewable energy providers expect demand to outstrip supply. “Even if just five gigawatts of data center capacity comes to India, which is a conservative estimate, you will need about 30-40 gigawatts of renewable power,” Kuldeep Jain, managing director and founder of CleanMax Enviro Energy Solutions Ltd., a major Indian renewables provider, told Bloomberg in an interview published on Friday. “It’s a case of demand…

articles.title: China’s Sufficient Gas Stocks Could Ease Winter Supply Concerns
articles.description: Chinese LNG buyers acted early to build gas stockpiles amid the Iran war, helping the world’s top LNG importer stock up enough inventories ahead of the winter, industry analysts have told Bloomberg. As of the end of September, China’s underground gas storage was 80% full, according to Rystad Energy’s analyst Xiong Wei. Lower demand for spot supply from China this winter could mean relief for other LNG customers in Asia and Europe, many of which have been struggling with high spot LNG prices and intensified competition for supply…

articles.title: South Korea Turns Back to Coal as LNG Crisis Deepens
articles.description: Soaring prices of spot LNG supply amid the lack of Middle Eastern deliveries have pushed South Korea to rely more on coal-fired power generation in the coming winter, despite its pledge to shift away from fossil fuels. Like all other Asian importers, South Korea, the world’s third-largest LNG buyer after China and Japan, has been hit by the Middle East crisis and the lack of Qatari LNG supply. Soaring spot LNG prices for supply not needing the Strait of Hormuz have made running gas-fired plants uneconomical compared to coal. In the…

articles.title: India Slashes Diesel Export Tax as Global Fuel Crunch Deepens
articles.description: India has nearly halved its export duty on diesel for the next two weeks while it hiked the levy on gasoline exports fivefold, effective October 16. The lower diesel export levy could encourage additional supply to the international market, which is reeling from a diesel crunch and price shocks, while the hike in the gasoline export duty appears to be intended to discourage gasoline exports. India reviews its export duty policy every fortnight to account for the prevailing domestic and international market conditions, including supply and prices.…

articles.title: Trump Condemns Ukraine’s Russian Refinery Strikes as a “Disgrace”
articles.description: Ukraine’s renewed attacks on Russian refineries are a “disgrace” and will only lead to higher prices, President Donald Trump has said in comments about the latest Ukrainian attack of a Rosneft facility in Ryazan. “All he’s doing is making the world oil price higher. Well, I think that’s a disgrace,” Trump told Newsmax in an interview. “There are a lot of targets you can hit, but when you shoot at diesel refineries where you make, you know, diesel oil, ‌and we need that, and the world needs that,…

articles.title: Global Fuel Oil Shortage Deepens as Middle East and Russia Supplies Collapse
articles.description: Global fuel oil supply is shrinking while demand for the fuel from the shipping industry remains robust, suggesting further supply pain down the road. Exports of high-sulfur fuel oil from the Middle East are running at a rate that is at least 800,000 tons a month lower than it was before the war, the head of Asian operations at Vitol said at an industry event. “Producers are paying higher freight rates and more risk premiums to shuttle cargoes out of Hormuz, recognising the importance of oil revenues to their national budgets,” Kieran…

articles.title: Oil Prices Head for Weekly Gain as Hormuz Attacks Rattle Markets
articles.description: Crude oil prices were on course to book a weekly gain earlier today, amid continuing Iranian strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a substantial inventory draw in the United States, at 8.56 million barrels for the week to October 9. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $105.48 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $97.40 per barrel. Both were off highs touched earlier in the week, but still higher than last Friday. “Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait…

articles.title: WTI Outpaces Brent as U.S. Crude Draw Ignites Fresh Buying
articles.description: Crude Oil Rallies as U.S. Inventory Draw Outruns Supply Relief November WTI crude oil futures are up sharply for the week through Thursday night. The gain did not come from one headline. The market has spent the week dealing with tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, renewed attacks on Russian refineries, emergency stock releases and fresh talk of legal oil moving on previously sanctioned vessels. The release and shipping headlines gave both sides of the trade something to work with. WTI got the stronger bid when the EIA reported a large U.S.…

articles.title: Oil Prices Diverge as Supply Risks Mount
articles.description: WTI surged 3% while Brent edged lower amid shifting shipping costs and tight global supplies.

articles.title: Standard Chartered: Trump's Russian Diesel Won't Add New Supply
articles.description: Oil prices were mixed in Thursday's trading session, with prospects of the United States easing restrictions on Russia's crude helping ease the international benchmark while attacks on vessels in the Middle East provided support. Brent crude for December delivery was down 0.2% to trade at $106 per barrel at 2.49 pm ET, while WTI crude for November delivery jumped 3.6% to trade at $98 per barrel. articles.title: The Diesel Crunch Will Persist Well into 2027
articles.description: The recent rise in crude oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz isn’t solving the world’s most pressing fuel problem—the diesel crunch and record diesel prices that start to feed into the wider economy. While Middle East crude oil flows are nearing pre-war levels, global diesel supply is much lower due to refinery constraints in the Middle East and Russia that the rest of the world cannot offset. The diesel squeeze hiked wholesale and retail prices to record highs in the middle of September as the market realized that crude oil…

articles.title: Exxon’s Oil Boom Could Keep Guyana’s Gas at Home
articles.description: Guyana has turned into something of an oil celebrity with billions of barrels discovered by Exxon off the coast of the tiny South American country. With the oil riches came gas, too, and there were plans to add LNG to Guyana’s export goods. Yet now the government is considering keeping the gas for the domestic market. Guyana’s crude oil exports are about to end the year on a high note and a daily rate of over 1 million barrels, according to a recent report by Bloomberg. It only took the country 10 years to go from no oil production…

articles.title: U.S. Nuclear Fuel Independence Edges Closer as Urenco Expansion Hits 75%
articles.description: The only commercial-scale uranium enrichment plant in the United States is now three-quarters of the way through its latest expansion, a milestone for the country's push to build out a domestic nuclear fuel supply chain. Urenco USA said Oct. 8 that the sixth of eight new centrifuge cascades at its National Enrichment Facility in New Mexico has started production, with the seventh due later this year and the last in spring 2027. As the Trump administration works to reestablish the country as the global leader in nuclear energy, cutting reliance…
